articles.title: Lions' Campbell has full movement in lower body after neck injury
articles.summary: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell says he has full movement in his lower body after he was taken to hospital with a neck injury during Sunday's NFL win over the Minnesota Vikings.
body: Campbell was face down on the turf and not moving after hitting tight end TJ Hockenson early in the fourth quarter of the Lions' 19-15 victory on Sunday.
The 26-year-old was evaluated by medical personnel before being strapped to a board and carefully lifted onto the cart to a round of applause.
Detroit's entire team and most of the coaching staff surrounded the cart.
Campbell offered his own injury update on Wednesday, noting that he also has movement in his upper body.

articles.title: Lions’ Jack Campbell making progress on movement in upper body after injury during game
articles.summary: Linebacker has ‘full movement in lower body’ 26-year-old was injured making tackle on Sunday. Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell says he has regained some movement in his body after sustaining a serious neck injury during his team’s win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.
body: The 26-year-old was treated for nine minutes on the field after making a tackle during Sunday’s game. Players from both teams were visibly distraught as Campbell received medical attention before he was taken for further treatment at a hospital in the Detroit area.

In a statement on Wednesday, Campbell said he is making progress in his recovery. “I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body,” Campbell, who remains hospitalized, said in the statement. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.”
On Monday, Lions coach Dan Campbell paid tribute to the former first-round pick’s contributions to the team.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy backs claim that LIV tried to 'destroy' DP World Tour
articles.summary: McIlroy: ‘LIV turned pro golf into an arms race’ DP chief executive: ‘We pay everyone on time’ Rory McIlroy voiced his support on Wednesday for the DP World Tour chief executive’s claim that LIV Golf’s goal was to “destroy” the European golf circuit.
body: The six-time major winner and former world No 1 spoke ⁠with the media on Wednesday before the Abu Dhabi Championship and was asked about Guy Kinnings’ recent interview with the Scotsman.

“But we also have to ⁠protect the tour against an entity who spent, so we are told, over $7bn, with one of their aims being to ‘destroy the DP World Tour’. I have heard that from so many different people they talked to, who I have known for ⁠over 30 years within the game and who I trust implicitly,” Kinnings said.

“Clearly, when you are faced with statements like that, and then ​people then ask why we are doing what we are doing with ‌our membership and invite policy for 2027, then ‌I think the answer becomes pretty obvious. Myself and everyone at the DP World Tour have a duty to our members to protect our tour. ‌We are proud of that and are proud that we treat everyone who works for the tour, whether that be staff, suppliers, contractors, everyone, with respect and dignity. We pay them and pay them on time. We look out for everyone.

articles.title: Defeat ends Djokovic's hopes of making ATP Finals
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic is out of the race to qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin after a second-round defeat by qualifier Rinky Hijikata at the Paris Masters.
body: It means Djokovic, 39, has failed to qualify for the event for only the second time in the past 20 seasons when fit.
The Serb likely needed to reach the semi-finals in Paris to qualify, although the draw had appeared to open up for him after two of his rivals for a place fell earlier in the day.
Despite a good start, Djokovic was unable to repel Australian world number 83 Hijikata in a 2-6 6-3 6-3 defeat.

As Hijikata lifted his level at the end of the second set and throughout the decider, Djokovic, who appeared laboured and to be struggling physically, produced a series of errors, bringing an end to his season.

articles.summary: For just the second time in 20 seasons, Novak Djokovic has failed to qualify for the season-ending ATP Finals after a shock defeat in the second round of the Rolex Paris Masters.
body: The 39-year-old, who also failed to make the 2017 edition due to a elbow injury, needed a run to the semi-finals to keep himself in with a chance of clinching a spot at the season-ending showpiece in Turin.
Djokovic, a seven-time champion in Paris, started well against 25-year-old Australian Rinky Hijikata, the world No 83, but faded badly in a 2-6 6-3 6-3 defeat.

With two places still available for the season-ending championship, Djokovic needed a run to the semi-finals in Paris to stay alive in his hopes, but his exit leaves the door open for the remaining contenders, including 12th-placed Taylor Fritz and 13th-placed Tommy Paul.
Hijikata told Sky Sports: "It took a lot. I was getting outplayed in the first set and had to hang tough.

body: Six years ago, Burnley were considered one of the best-run clubs in the country.
The Clarets were debt free, with £41.65m cash in the bank, and enjoying their fifth successive season of Premier League football.
Now they sit in the Championship relegation zone, with concerns over debt and the way the Clarets were bought by ALK Capital using loans and the club's own money.
Fans have been very concerned about what the future holds - although on Wednesday there was some rare positive news in the club's accounts.

articles.title: Olympic medallist Barbosu banned for doping violation
articles.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport upholds a decision to ban Olympic bronze medallist Ana Barbosu for two years after three whereabouts failures.
body: Olympic bronze medallist Ana Barbosu has been given a two-year ban for three whereabouts failures for anti-doping tests.

Romanian Barbosu, who won bronze in the women's floor final at the Paris Games in 2024, was initially suspended by the International Testing Agency (ITA) in May for missing three tests between September and December 2025.
Barbosu, 20, appealed against the decision to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), who upheld the ruling after a hearing in August.
Her ban will be in place for two years from 5 May 2026, the date she was provisionally suspended.

articles.title: Goalkeeper Owono posts of 'most difficult days' after De Miguel's death from collision
articles.summary: Jesus Owono says he is going through the most difficult ‌days of his life in a statement released by his club FC Andorra on Wednesday, following the death of ‌Tenerife forward Jesus De Miguel.
body: The Tenerife forward died on Tuesday morning following a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

Owono was sent off for the clash having raced from his goal and struck 30-year-old De Miguel at force, with the Tenerife player subsequently suffering a cardiac arrest after being taken into intensive care.

"These are the most difficult days of my life," ‌Owono said in a statement. "I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to ​process what has happened. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.
"But right now, honestly, ​I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the ⁠pain we are experiencing. Rest in ⁠peace, Jesus."

articles.title: Week 9 Fantasy Football D/ST Rankings: Lamar Jackson's Injury And Justin Herbert's Existence Have A Big Impact
articles.summary: While the overwhelming majority of attention in fantasy football focuses on the offensive stars in the league, we still have to pay attention to defense and special teams as well.
body: This is a dream matchup for the Jaguars' defense on Thursday Night Football against the Baltimore Ravens on a short week. These teams will face off on Thursday Night Football, just four days after the Ravens lost their starting quarterback, Lamar Jackson, and their backup, Tyler Huntley.

That leaves a strong Jaguars' defense to pick apart third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano. This one could get really ugly, and we expect the Jacksonville defense to destroy the Ravens' offense on Thursday.

The Texans have the pleasure of playing against the spiraling Justin Herbert this week. The Chargers' offense has been a disaster, and Herbert has been woefully bad. Over the past two games, he has thrown three interceptions and zero touchdowns, bringing his season total to five touchdowns and 10 interceptions, while averaging less than 200 passing yards per game, despite constantly playing from behind and losing every single game.
Houston is going to eat Herbert and this offense alive. Only Joe Fagnano could keep Houston from being the top defense in Week 9. It will be a huge day for Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter.

articles.title: CJ Carr faces defining moment as Notre Dame's CFP hopes ride on showdown vs. No. 1 Miami
articles.summary: The Fighting Irish quarterback has struggled against ranked opponents, but Miami's vulnerable secondary offers the perfect stage to save Notre Dame's playoff hopes
body: When the College Football Playoff rankings were released on Tuesday, Notre Dame was one of the biggest losers in the field. The Fighting Irish sit at No. 11 with only one loss against No. 9 BYU, but without quality wins to their name.

One year after finishing as the first team out of the College Football Playoff, the Fighting Irish are firmly on the bubble. Notre Dame projects as the last team in and can't afford any more slip-ups.
Now, a Saturday matchup against No. 1 Miami becomes a must-win game. And more importantly, it marks the most important game of quarterback CJ Carr's career.

Carr has been one of the steadiest quarterbacks in college football, completing 67% of his passes with an 18-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio. His 82.7 QBR is eighth-best in college football, adjusted for competition. But in the Fighting Irish's lone quality matchup against the Cougars, Carr was lackluster.
